leads.name: Chene de Bois-Genoud

location.address: Domaine/Le Castel de Bois-Genoud, west of Lausanne near Crissier/Romanel-sur-Lausanne

leads.reason: Strong candidate on paper: City of Lausanne's own heritage-tree page gives 500 years old, girth roughly 700-800cm, height 18m, restored by the municipality in 1999, 'the last representative of four centuries-old oaks' in an 18th-century park by the same Parisian landscape architect who designed Mon Repos, and it appears in Henri Badoux's 1925 book on the canton's notable trees. NOT SHIPPED because access could not be confirmed this pass: Bois-Genoud/Le Castel appears to be a private domain now used partly as an event/wedding venue (myvaud.ch / vaud.ch tourism listing), and a direct fetch to confirm public access 404'd. Also possibly outside Lausanne's own municipal boundary (nearer Crissier or Romanel-sur-Lausanne, needs distance/transit check). A future pass should confirm whether the park (as opposed to the Castel building) is open to casual visitors before this ships.

leads.name: Cedre d'Ansermet
leads.reason: Only about 100 years old ('still young' per the city's own description), girth 439cm, height 20m. A fine specimen but not old enough or singular enough on its own to clear the bar without a stronger why-go; single-sourced (the municipal page only). Keep as a filler candidate if the city page needs a fourth or fifth tree later.

leads.name: Sauvabelin venerable oaks
leads.species: Oak, species and individual specimen not identified

location.address: Bois de Sauvabelin nature reserve, Lausanne

leads.reason: A search result described Sauvabelin as home to 'venerable oaks, some already over three centuries old' but did not name an individual specimen with a precise location. Sauvabelin is a well-known, easily walkable, publicly accessible forest reserve close to central Lausanne (also home to a lake, a famous wooden observation tower and a vivarium), and is worth a dedicated follow-up search for a specific named oak.
leads.source: search summary only, page not directly fetched this pass; treat the '300 years' figure as unconfirmed until read on a real page per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's rule on search summaries

leads.name: Lausanne's other named heritage trees (still uninvestigated)
leads.reason: The City of Lausanne's 'patrimoine arbore' series (lausanne.ch/vie-pratique/nature/patrimoine-arbore/arbres.html) lists 32 named trees in total. A continuation pass on 2026-09-11 opened and shipped 4 more (chene-du-musee-olympique, cedre-du-denantou, ginkgo-de-mon-repos, tilleul-de-bon-abri, plus noyer-de-la-campagne-rohner), on top of the 3 already published and the 2 above. Still unopened: le charme de la Tour Haldimand, le platane des Mouettes, le platane de Rhodanie, le Saule des Pyramides, le cedre de la Vaudoise, le sapin de Montriond, le cedre de Grancy, le noyer de Contigny, le murier de Montoie, le pin de Montelly, le chene vert de l'Art brut, l'if de la promenade Lucienne-Schnegg, le marronnier de la Barre, le tulipier de la Campagne, le pin des Escaliers du Marche, le cedre a encens de Rumine, le platane du Valentin, le cedre du Pre-du-Marche, le cedre de Collonges, le cedre du Presbytere, le sequoia des Bergieres, les platanes du Desert, le tilleul de la Chapelle, le chene de la Fauvette. URL pattern: lausanne.ch/vie-pratique/nature/patrimoine-arbore/arbres/[slug].html. A dedicated follow-up pass could very likely take this city well past ten trees.

notes: Verification pass 2026-09-11 (continuation): the City of Lausanne's own 'patrimoine arbore' series, combined with Lausanne Tourisme's own 'A walk to discover Lausanne's most beautiful trees' article (independently covering 5 named trees on the same walk, with closely matching figures), gave two independent official/semi-official sources for 5 more trees in one pass: the Oak of the Olympic Museum (Samaranch story, 200 years), the Cedar of Lebanon of Parc Denantou (250 years), the Ginkgo of Parc de Mon Repos (160 years, joins the already-published sequoia in the same park), the Linden of Bon-Abri (age disputed between sources, 160 vs 260 years, flagged), and the Black Walnut of Campagne Rohner (150 years, flagged for a location-name discrepancy between the two sources). City now has 8 verified trees against the 4-tree floor. No Swiss/Vaud register was found for Lausanne per OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md (only Geneva was scouted and imported in the Swiss pass of 2026-08-15). Still 24 named heritage-tree pages unopened (see lead above); Sauvabelin's named venerable oak(s) also still unconfirmed.
